adaptive_attempts.hypothesis: Inherited model misclassifies development cracks as warping. Amplifying 64 channels with the strongest positive crack-versus-warp activation contrast may preserve crack evidence through the last blocks. This is a small diagnostic perturbation, chosen after reading the inherited confusion matrices.

Probe 01 moved a crack error from warping to layer shift without fixing it. Rather than amplify existing channels, add a development-derived crack correction at block 9, before inherited block 10. Fit zero desired change for other development cases; use stronger regularization than the prior grid to reduce memorization.

Probe 02 changed no decisions and had weight-delta norm 0.01035. Test the same direction at norm about 0.414, still below the inherited edit norm 1.132, to distinguish insufficient amplitude from a useless direction. Chosen after probe 02 feedback, not a predeclared sweep.

Probe 03 fixed 3 selection cracks but made 4 layer-shift samples false cracks. Keep the crack correction direction while fitting a counter-direction on development layer-shift samples to reduce their crack logit. Use only development labels to fit; same block and strength isolate this protection change.

Probe 04 protection dominated: patch norm increased from 0.414 to 1.476 and crack selection fell to 2/10. Reduce only protection by 10x while preserving the useful crack direction. This tests whether mild class-specific protection can recover the layer-shift regressions without erasing crack evidence.

Both strong and weak crack-only protection failed to improve held-out selection. Abandon the one-class hypothesis: fit a simultaneous residual correction for all remaining development mistakes so layer-shift errors receive their own positive correction. Use block 9 before inherited block 10, moderate gain, and the previously useful ridge fraction.

Probe 06 achieved perfect development classification but selection dropped to 28/40: over-adaptation. Reduce only intervention amplitude to 30%, producing expected norm about 0.384, to test a conservative version. If it cannot improve selection, reject this branch and retain the inherited checkpoint.
